title: Quant exec path: kernel & scheduling constraints for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ
content:
Purpose:
This doc lays out execution-path constraints, kernel requirements, and scheduler interactions for shipping quantized inference (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) in the serving runtime. Goal is to enumerate safe kernel/format combinations, memory layout expectations, KV-cache interaction patterns, fallback behaviors, and test/telemetry needed before enabling each quantized path in hosted and dedicated tiers.

Scope and definitions:
- INT8: symmetric and asymmetric int8 kernels (per-tensor and per-channel scales).
- FP8: e4m3 and e5m2 formats where applicable; fused accumulators expectations.
- GPTQ: post-training quantized weights (per-channel scales, often 4-bit/8-bit hybrid layout), with dequant-on-the-fly or fused kernels.
- AWQ: advanced weight quantization (mixed bitwidth block quant) with custom permutation/layouts.
- Execution path: combination of kernel implementation (CUDA/ROCm/CPU), memory layout of weights/activation, scheduling constraints (batching/streaming), and runtime flags (fallback, compatibility checks).

High-level constraints (must be enforced by runtime before selecting a path):
1) Kernel capability discovery: At startup and during node attach, the runtime must advertise supported quant formats per device and per driver (e.g., nvprims for INT8, cublasLt vs custom kernels for FP8). Capability vector fields: device_id, cuda_compute_capability, driver_version, kernel_library_version, supported_formats (list), max_seq_len_per_stream, fused_matmul_bias_activation_supported (bool).
2) Weight layout canonicalization: Each quant format must map to a canonical in-memory descriptor that kernels agree on. Descriptor fields (string metadata attached to model artifact): element_type, block_size, block_order, scale_storage (per_channel|per_tensor), zero_point_scheme (if any), backing_buffer_alignment. Runtime will reject model if descriptor incompatible with kernel.
3) Runtime alignment and padding: INT8/GPTQ/AWQ block sizes require 32/64-byte alignment for efficient loads. Kernels assume final dim padded to block multiples (e.g., 32 for int8-gemm microtiles). Scheduler must ensure allocations include padding.
4) KV cache compatibility: Quantized models that perform KV cache from activations require exact fp32/ fp16 accumulator semantics or explicitly defined accumulation mode. For FP8-backed activations, kernels must provide an accumulator path that produces FP16/FP32 keys/values before storing in KV cache. If accumulator path not available, runtime must route requests to a compatible model variant (fallback).
5) Batching & continuous decoding: Some quant kernels disable large continuous batching because of register pressure. The scheduler should enforce a per-kernel max_concurrent_tokens threshold. If scheduling would exceed threshold, fall back to slower but safe path (e.g., fp16 kernel).
6) Determinism & RNG: FP8 and highly quantized paths may be nondeterministic across driver versions due to fused kernels. For SLOs that require determinism (tests/benchmarks/customer opt-in), runtime must pin kernel versions or force full-precision path.

Kernel-level constraints (per-format):
A. INT8 (per-channel) kernels:
- Required: per-channel scale lookup and requantize step, bias in FP32/FP16, support for asymmetric zero-point if model uses it.
- Memory: weights stored as [out_block, in_block] with per-out-channel scale array, 16-byte aligned scales.
- Activation path: activations typically fp16 or fp32 input; kernel does fp16->int8 quantize or assumes pre-quantized inputs. Runtime must negotiate whether quantize-on-input is allowed (adds latency).
- KV cache: KV store must accept keys/values in fp16 or fp32 only; if kernel accumulates to fp32 then stores float.
- Fallback triggers: scale mismatch (per-tensor vs per-channel), zero-point present but kernel doesn't support it, or device lacking optimized int8 microkernels.

B. FP8 kernels (e4m3 / e5m2):
- Required: per-tensor exponent bias handling, fused cast->accumulate sequences.
- Accumulators: must provide fp16/fp32 accumulation to preserve decoder state precision when writing to KV cache. Documented API: kernel.accumulate_mode = "fp16" | "fp32".
- Numeric checks: runtime must run a small warmup (N=16 tokens) comparing FP8 path vs fp16 baseline for mismatch ratio; if mismatch > configurable threshold, disable FP8 for that model.
- Scheduling: FP8 kernels may have strict max_seq_len due to fused operator register pressure. Enforce via kernel metadata.

C. GPTQ (4-bit/8-bit hybrid) kernels:
- Layout: weights stored in packed bitstreams with per-block scales and optional permutation tables. Descriptor must include bitwidth map by block.
- On-the-fly dequant: kernel may dequant blocks into shared workspace; workspace size must be bounded and provided in kernel metadata. Scheduler needs to ensure memory reservation for workspace per-stream.
- Warm caches: first few requests may incur overhead dequanting hot blocks; scheduler should prefer warm-start for canary testing and load tests.
- KV cache: keys/values must be produced as fp16/fp32 by dequant path. If streaming decode requires producing keys per step with low latency, kernel must support incremental dequant of only active blocks.
- Fallbacks: if workspace allocation fails, or permutation tables not supported on device, route to fallback fp16 kernel.

D. AWQ (mixed-block advanced quant):
- Variability: AWQ uses blockwise mixed bitwidths and possibly reorderings. Runtime must validate block descriptors against kernel capability table (kernel_cap.supports_awq_vX).
- Permutation handling: If AWQ uses blocked permutations, kernel either supports in-kernel permutation or runtime must pre-permute weights on load. Pre-permutation is expensive but one-time at model load.
- Scheduling note: AWQ's memory footprint smaller, but compute pattern is irregular; scheduling should avoid overcommit of concurrent streams. Provide conservative concurrency defaults.

Compatibility matrix (runtime MUST enforce):
- Device lacking cublasLt FP8 -> FP8 disabled.
- Device lacking custom int8 microkernels -> INT8 disabled or fallback to fp16.
- GPTQ/AWQ packed-block support requires kernel_lib >= X.Y.Z and driver >= D.D.D.
- If model metadata requests kv_cache_store_type=quantized (i.e., store compressed keys), runtime must reject unless explicit experimental flag set and the cluster certifies persistence/compatibility.

Scheduler interaction patterns and policies:
1) Kernel metadata registration: Each kernel implementation registers a metadata blob to the scheduler at bootstrap with fields: supported_formats, max_concurrent_streams, workspace_per_stream_bytes, max_seq_len, prefers_prequantized_inputs (bool), requires_zero_point_support (bool). Scheduler uses these to build a capability matrix per node.
2) Fast path selection logic (pseudocode):
   - Candidate_kernels = kernels_that_support(model.format)
   - Filter by device.available_memory >= workspace_per_stream_bytes * concurrency
   - Filter by max_seq_len >= requested_seq_len
   - Rank by estimated_token_ms_per_unit (from telemetry) and by cost_model
   - If top_candidate meets latency SLO and passes warmup numeric test -> select
   - Else try next candidate or route to fp16 fallback
3) Admission control: For quant kernels with tight resource requirements (e.g., GPTQ workspace), the scheduler enforces a per-device admission token bucket. Admission tokens consumed per-request proportional to seq_len*batch_size. Helps preserve headroom for latency-critical requests.
4) Canary and warmup: When enabling a new quant kernel/model combo, the scheduler must bias a small percent (default 2%) of requests for numerical drift checks comparing output logits to baseline. Canary requests are tagged and routed to both quant and baseline paths; results collected and drift metric computed.

KV cache specifics and edge cases:
- Storage format: Always canonicalize KV cache on-disk/network as fp16 or fp32. Do NOT persist quantized KV to cluster cache unless experimental flag. Reason: quantization artifacts amplify across long context and complicate rollbacks.
- Interop: If a model variant is quantized but the serving app expects to resume contexts produced by a fp16 model, runtime must map and potentially dequantize keys. This mapping adds CPU/GPU work and must be included in cost model.
- Cache migration: Provide a migration tool that reads fp16 cached keys and re-encodes for quantized model if customer enables experimental KV-store-compressed mode.

Fallback semantics and error handling:
- Soft fallback: If numeric warmup drift > threshold OR runtime resource shortfall detected -> transparently route new requests to fallback path (fp16). Logged with tag quant_fallback_reason. Not exposed to users except via observability.
- Hard fallback: If kernel fails on execution (CUDA error, misaligned buffer), abort request, mark node unhealthy for X minutes, and route traffic elsewhere. Capture core dump and stack to /artifacts for offline debugging.

Telemetry and testing requirements before GA:
- Per-format telemetry: mean/median token latency, p50/p95/p99, assess throughput tokens/sec, memory per stream, failure rate, fallback rate, numeric drift percentiles (compared to baseline).
- Regression tests: unit tests for kernel descriptors, synthetic microbenchmarks across seq_len and batch size grid, and long-context accumulation tests for KV correctness.
- Numerical tests: run N=500 in-distribution prompts comparing logits/next-token distributions between quant path and fp16 with thresholds per-format (INT8 < 0.2% top-1 mismatch; FP8 < 0.5% top-1 mismatch; GPTQ/AWQ thresholds set per-model during onboarding).
- Deployment tests: staged rollout 0 -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated numeric monitors gating next percentage.

Model artifact metadata requirements (must be present):
- quant_format: one of [INT8, FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2, GPTQ, AWQ, NONE]
- descriptor_version: semver string
- block_size / bitwidth_map: for GPTQ/AWQ
- kernel_compat: list of kernel_lib version strings certified
- kv_cache_compat: boolean (true if safe to persist quantized KV)

Operational checklist to enable a new quant format on hosted cluster:
- [ ] Certify kernels on target device families (ampere, ada, MI100, etc.)
- [ ] Add kernel metadata to capability registry and CI smoke tests
- [ ] Implement warmup numeric test harness and canary routing hooks
- [ ] Add admission token accounting to scheduler
- [ ] Add observability panels: drift, fallback reasons, per-model quant telemetry
- [ ] Update model onboarding docs and mandatory artifact metadata fields

Open questions / risks:
- How to support cross-node KV cache sharing when different nodes have different quant capabilities? (current plan: normalize KV on source to fp16 before sharing)
- Can we permit persistent quantized KV in future? Requires long-term study of drift accumulation and snapshot semantics.
- Cost model: quant paths save memory/compute but may increase per-request dequant overhead. Need experiments to model break-even workloads.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: implement kernel metadata registration changes (PI-1)
- Miguel: add warmup numeric harness and early telemetry (PI-1)
- Lina: schedule admission token prototype in scheduler service (PI-2)
- Devon: design canary dashboards and fallback alerting (PI-1)

Appendix: quick checklist for engineers adding a kernel:
1) Add kernel implementation + unit tests to repo.
2) Publish kernel metadata JSON following runtime schema.
3) Include model artifact examples (small quant model with descriptor).
4) Add CI smoke tests verifying kernel loads and the warmup numeric test passes on a small dataset.
